incidents.name: Generic
incidents.note: Common in DeFi vault implementations. See SWC-101.

initial_state.rounding_direction: ⚠️ Rounds DOWN on both deposit and withdraw

steps.description: Attacker first deposits a tiny amount (1 wei of USDC) to receive 1 share, then donates 1,000,000 USDC directly to the vault (not through deposit). This inflates the share price so that 1 share = ~1,000,001 USDC. Now any deposit smaller than 1,000,001 USDC will mint 0 shares due to rounding down.

Victim users deposit USDC into the vault, expecting to receive proportional shares. A user depositing 500,000 USDC receives 0 shares because the rounding math truncates to zero. Their 500,000 USDC is added to the vault's total assets, further enriching the attacker's single share.

Alternatively, without waiting for victims, the attacker can exploit rounding in a loop. By depositing amounts just below the rounding threshold and immediately withdrawing, the attacker can extract tiny amounts of value each iteration due to asymmetric rounding between deposit and withdrawal.

After accumulating victim deposits (or running the rounding loop), the attacker redeems their single share. Since they hold 100% of the shares, they receive the entire vault balance — their original deposit plus all the value stolen from victims through rounding.

The attack exploited the ERC-4626 vault's rounding behavior combined with share price inflation. Mitigations include: implementing virtual shares/assets offset, enforcing minimum deposit amounts, rounding in favor of the vault on deposits and in favor of users on withdrawals, and using OpenZeppelin's ERC4626 with built-in inflation attack protection.

state_changes.fix_3: ✓ Round UP on deposit (mint fewer shares), DOWN on withdraw
state_changes.fix_4: ✓ Use OpenZeppelin ERC4626 with built-in protection
